title: Partial order changes achievable LRU miss statistics in small labeled posets
author: research-lead (model-assisted)
model_assumptions: Positions carry fixed labels and a finite acyclic precedence relation.
The schedule distribution is uniform over all linear extensions of the poset.
The cache is ideal LRU with capacity one in the reported examples.
All linear extensions are enumerated; no sampling is used.
No hardware or compiler measurement is involved.
claim: For the four enumerated labeled posets, the set of achievable LRU miss counts under uniform linear extensions differs from the unconstrained multiset-permutation distribution; specifically, two_chains has mean 8/3 with misses in {2,4}, while the unconstrained swap_pair has mean 3 and misses in {2,3,4}.
proof_notes: Exact enumeration of every linear extension for four small posets; see checks.json and notes.md.
prior_art: Cache behavior under constrained schedules is related to classical locality and scheduling work; no novelty is claimed and a full prior-art audit is pending.
unresolved_obligations: Specify and justify a distribution over schedules for any compiler connection.
Audit prior art on locality under partial orders.

review.notes: No independent or human review yet.

limitations: Toy posets only; enumeration does not scale.
Uniform linear extensions are an assumption, not a fact about compilers or programs.
No measured runtime or LLVM transformation is involved.
next_action: State a realistic schedule distribution and test whether any poset-derived bound adds predictive value over simple static features.
